title: You Have to Show You Care Before Delivering a Tough Message
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece tackles the challenge of delivering difficult feedback without losing the other person's trust or goodwill. It argues the fix isn't softening the content of the message but anchoring it upfront with a stated intent to help, which lets the recipient feel respected even while hearing unwelcome news. Several paired examples contrast a blunt opening with a care-first opening that leads with the same substance. The piece closes by noting that leaders who can master this delivery style tend to be viewed favorably for promotion.
points: Delivering tough messages well while still being liked afterward is described as a rare leadership skill.
The fix is leading with stated intent to help before delivering the substance of the message.
Several sample phrasings show how to frame difficult feedback around care and support.
Leaders who can deliver hard messages gracefully tend to be favored for promotion.
quotes: Saying difficult things in such a way that people like you after the conversation is among the rarest of leadership skills.
The easier pathway is to avoid the conversation altogether, or to get it over with as quickly as possible.
They begin difficult conversations by clarifying their intent to help, guide, and support the other party.
I’m raising this because I want you to succeed here, and this issue will hold you back if we don’t address it.
Mastering the skill of communicating with care and support before offering unpleasant news can be a huge difference maker for both parties.
Leaders who can convey a tough message with a graceful and compassionate style typically rise quickly in organizations.
